title: Session handoff: 0.9.0 shipped, five findings open, and the installed 0.7.1 is deliberate
description:
Handoff at recycle, 2026-09-19. Written for a successor with no memory of this session. The tracker and the repository outrank this record; verify before acting.

RELEASE: quest 0.9.0 IS PUBLISHED AND VERIFIED. Wrapper plus all six platform packages on npm. main = v0.9.0^{commit} = e8eeaf1418c45219c829e6691046c5f03a5a0e24. Verified by a real consumer install rather than the publisher exit code: npm install @opum-ai/quest@0.9.0 resolves quest-darwin-arm64, runs, reports 0.9.0, and returns the new QCLI-346 validation error for a taken --id. main has since been promoted to 051ecab (tracker and docs only, no shipped source), and v0.9.0 still peels to e8eeaf1 where it always pointed.

Why the number skipped 0.8.0: 0.8.0 was frozen, tagged at 9d91fc35 and never published, then 15 commits landed after the freeze. The tag was NOT re-pointed -- quest-web runs a live link gate against this repository and opum-marketplace re-resolves tag to commit to tree against a recorded baseline -- so the content shipped under the next unclaimed number, per the 0.6.1-to-0.6.2 precedent.

THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS RECORD, because the obvious action is wrong: THE GLOBALLY INSTALLED quest ON THIS MACHINE IS 0.7.1 AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. Do not run npm install -g @opum-ai/quest@0.9.0 to fix it. That global install is what opum-cli-e2e docs gate and Tracker integrity jobs resolve against, and what lore check shells out to. Swapping it mid-flight moves rows in their runs with nothing in the output explaining why, and invalidates the control baseline they measured at 405/0/5. They will upgrade it themselves once their pair baseline is cut, so the move is recorded as a deliberate step rather than discovered as a discrepancy. A successor reading 0.7.1 as staleness and helpfully fixing it breaks another repository gates.

FIVE FINDINGS OPEN, all with evidence already in their records:
- QCLI-286 a rolled-forward CHANGELOG section swallows later fixes. It came true a second time and is deliberately NOT closed: its criteria require a mechanism implemented, documented in the runbook and running in CI, and none of that exists. It carries the detector shape -- git log <last tag>..HEAD -- src/ returned exactly 5 of 15 commits with no false positives.
- QCLI-348 quest browser outlives its workspace. Four daemons measured, one per matrix run, bound by workspace token to their runs. opum-cli-e2e will reap them on their next run; the evidence is in the task, not in the processes.
- QCLI-349 publish-release reports a present-but-unreadable Keychain credential as an absent one. Exit 36, errSecInteractionNotAllowed. High priority: it stalls a release and points at the opposite remedy.
- QCLI-350 the publisher says published and verified about the wrapper while verifying the platform packages, and names two of four visibility states.
- QCLI-351 the shipped task-creation guide should warn that a count baked into an acceptance criterion goes stale.

TWO THINGS A SUCCESSOR WOULD OTHERWISE RE-LEARN THE HARD WAY. Both are now in CLAUDE.md and the release runbook, which is where a session looks at publish time, so read those rather than this. First: no stored token found at publish time means the keychain is LOCKED, not empty -- check presence with security find-generic-password -s npm-opum-ai-publish (exit 0 present, 44 missing) and have the owner run security unlock-keychain at a terminal. No OTP is needed on the token route. Second: npm read lag routinely produces the exact signature the runbook attributes to a STAGED version -- absent from versions, absent from time, time.modified unchanged. It happened twice in this release and neither was staged. Only a 409 is positive evidence.

A MISTAKE WORTH NOT REPEATING: tracker edits made on dev and left uncommitted were destroyed by git reset --hard origin/dev during branch setup. Six checked criteria and a long note had to be reconstructed. Tracker writes are working-tree changes; make them on a branch and commit them promptly.

STATE AT HANDOFF: dev and main aligned at 051ecab before this commit, zero In Progress, no open PRs, clean tree, sdlc-audit clean apart from the unpromoted finding this promotion cleared. Nothing is blocked and nothing is waiting on a decision.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A successor can state, without re-deriving it, that 0.9.0 is published and that the installed 0.7.1 is deliberate rather than stale.
This task is closed once a successor has read it, or superseded by the next handoff -- it is a note, not work.

The stop is a renewal, not a blocker -- which is the distinction the handoff skill draws, and getting it wrong would have a successor hunting for an obstacle that does not exist.

FIVE FINDINGS OPEN, evidence already in each record, none blocked on anything: QCLI-286 (changelog check; deliberately not closed because its criteria require an implemented CI gate), QCLI-348 (browser leak, four daemons measured one per run), QCLI-349 (Keychain credential reported as absent when it is merely unreadable -- highest value, it stalls a release and points at the opposite remedy), QCLI-350 (publisher verification names the wrong object; two of four visibility states), QCLI-351 (shipped task-creation guide should warn about counts in criteria).
